the model says the meaning changed: A requirement whose proof is marked post_merge is now skipped by unconfirmed_proofs, so a merge into main no longer refuses it until its proof is shown and the owner confirms it, which weakens EX-7 and the statement that the merge refuses each delivered requirement.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: You said work is done only once you have been shown it working the way you chose, that the merge is refused until then, and that a missing proof must not get through with only a mention. The requirement says the same: a merge into main refuses each requirement it delivers until its proof is shown and you confirm it. So the requirement and your intent still agree.

The change adds a new kind of proof, marked "post-merge", for things that can only be shown once the branch is in main, such as a live session of the plugin reloaded from main. The merge check now skips these proofs completely. The branch lands without the proof being shown or confirmed, and the landing names the proof. The next turn then tells the agent to show it and ask you. For these proofs, the merge no longer waits, which goes against the rule you set.

What is unclear is whether you wanted this exception. The code cites another requirement (SR-341) as the reason, and the proof would have to be agreed as post-merge when it is chosen. That suggests a deliberate design, and without it such proofs could never get past the merge. But nothing here shows that you confirmed that exception, and no prompt from you was logged for the turn that probably made the change. Separately, the change also lets a "yes" you gave under a record's old number still count after a renumber, as long as the wording is unchanged. That part does not weaken the rule.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the exception: a proof you agreed as post-merge when choosing it does not hold the merge, but must be shown and confirmed right after landing. Reword the requirement and your intent to say so.") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the exception, but only if you confirm each post-merge proof yourself through the question tool when it is chosen, so the agent can never mark one alone. Reword to match.") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the exception: every proof holds the merge until it is shown and confirmed, even if that means finding another way to show it before landing.") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (iaso stale card SR-253#3 --consequences "..." --why "...")
